title.value: Extracting Person Names from User Generated Text: Named-Entity Recognition for Combating Human Trafficking
title.justification: The paper focuses on developing a Named-Entity Recognition system to extract person names from text related to combating human trafficking.
title.quote: In this paper, we pro- pose NEAT (Name Extraction Against Trafficking) for extracting person names. It effec- tively combines classic rule-based and dictionary extractors with a contextualized language model to capture ambiguous names.

extractions.description: The paper presents NEAT, a Named-Entity Recognition (NER) approach designed to extract person names from noisy and adversarial texts found in online escort advertisements. This is crucial for combating human trafficking, as extracting multiple names in such ads can be indicative of trafficking, providing valuable insights for law enforcement.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of this paper is the development of an NER system to combat human trafficking by extracting person names from online advertisements, which does not directly relate to climate or ecological sustainable development goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Named-Entity Recognition (NER) on escort ads is challenging because the text can be noisy, colloquial and often lacking proper grammar and punctuation.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on climate or ecological sustainable development topics but rather on human trafficking, which is a significant human rights issue not directly linked to environmental sustainability.
primary_category.quote: Thus, extracting person names from the text of these ads can provide valuable clues for further analysis...One of the key tasks in this domain is extracting information from the online escort ads e.g. names, phone numbers, locations, prices and activity types.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address climate or ecological sustainable development themes in any secondary capacity. It remains focused on human trafficking detection and law enforcement applications.
secondary_categories.quote: While the general task of Named Entity Recognition (NER) usually includes diverse entities such as person names, organizations, and ge- olocations, in this paper, we focus on person name extraction from escort ads for combating human trafficking.

primary_sub_category.justification: Since the paper's focus is not aligned with any predefined sub-categories related to climate or ecological sustainable development, it cannot be categorized under any specific sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: Therefore, simple rule-based extractors or machine learning models that are context-based alone will fail in several instances in this domain.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary climate or ecological sustainable development themes are present in the paper, remaining strictly within the scope of human trafficking concerns.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: NEAT shows 19% improvement on average in the F1 classification score for name extraction compared to previous state-of-the-art in two domain-specific datasets.

applications.justification: The application of the paper is targeted towards law enforcement for combating human trafficking by improving person name extraction in escort ads using NER.
applications.quote: Technology has been a critical tool for traffickers to recruit, advertise and exploit victims...we focus on person name extraction from escort ads for combating human trafficking.

new_primary_category.justification: There is no need for a new climate or ecological sustainable development category as the paper does not address such themes.
new_primary_category.quote: Named-Entity Recognition (NER) on escort ads is challenging because the text can be noisy, colloquial and often lacking proper grammar and punctuation.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper's content does not warrant the creation of a new sub-category under climate or ecological sustainable development as it does not relate to this field.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: This work suffers from the shortcomings of any rule-based approaches as discussed before.
